title: Aspect 6: Future Tense (Two Futures)
description: Russian has two futures, one for each aspect. Imperfective: буду + infinitive. Perfective: present-tense conjugation of the perfective verb.
descriptionRussian: В русском языке два будущих времени. НСВ: буду + инфинитив. СВ: личные формы перфективного глагола.
intro: Aspect is not a past-tense thing. It reaches into the future too, and it is why Russian has two futures where English has one. The choice is exactly the one you have been making for three lessons, pointed forwards instead of backwards. What changes is only the machinery: one aspect builds its future with a helper verb, the other with plain endings.
rules: Imperfective future: быть (in future) + imperfective infinitive. Я буду читать; ты будешь читать; etc.
Perfective future: present-tense conjugation FORMS of the perfective verb. The forms look like present tense but always have future meaning, because the perfective has no real present.
Aspect choice in the future follows the same rules as the past. Duration / habit → imperfective future. Completion / single event → perfective future.
examples: Завтра я буду читать книгу. (Tomorrow I will be reading the book.) НСВ future.
Завтра я прочитаю книгу. (Tomorrow I will read the book through.) СВ future.
Маша будет готовить обед каждый день. (Masha will cook dinner every day.) Habit → НСВ future.
Маша приготовит обед к семи часам. (Masha will have dinner ready by seven.) Deadline → СВ future.
Они будут писать статьи всё лето. (They will be writing articles all summer.) Duration → НСВ future.
Они напишут статью за неделю. (They will write the article in a week.) За + acc → СВ future.

rows.label: Imperfective future
cells: буду / будешь / будет / будем / будете / будут + impf infinitive

rows.label: Choice rule
cells: Duration / habit → impf future; completion → perf future

items.promptEnglish: Tomorrow I (m) will read the book through.
items.hint: 'Read it through' suggests a single completed event. Future tense, perfective.
items.explanation: 'Read the book through' marks completion: single completed event. Perfective future is the present-tense conjugation of the perfective verb: прочитаю (1sg).

items.promptEnglish: Tomorrow I (m) will be reading all day.
items.hint: 'All day' is a duration cue. Imperfective future form is...?
items.explanation: 'Весь день' is a duration cue, locking in the imperfective. Imperfective future = буду + impf infinitive → буду читать.

items.hint: Single completed cooking event in the future. Perfective future, 3sg form (same form across genders).
items.explanation: A single completed cooking event in the future: perfective future. Perfective future uses present-tense forms of the perfective verb: приготовит (3sg).

items.promptEnglish: They will write articles every day.
items.hint: 'Every day' is a habit cue. Imperfective future, plural.
items.explanation: 'Каждый день' is a habit cue, locking in the imperfective. Imperfective future = будут (plural) + impf infinitive писать.

items.promptEnglish: I (m) will have the soup ready by lunch.
items.hint: 'К обеду' (by lunch) is a deadline cue. Perfective future, 1sg.
items.explanation: 'К обеду' is a deadline cue (Lesson 5), locking in the perfective. Perfective future: приготовлю (1sg, present-conjugation form of the perfective).

items.promptEnglish: Tomorrow Lena will be writing all morning.
items.hint: 'Всё утро' is a duration. Which future goes with a process?
items.explanation: A duration phrase (всё утро) calls for the imperfective future: будет писать.

items.promptEnglish: Tomorrow Anton will finish the article.
items.hint: One finished result tomorrow. Which future signals completion?
items.explanation: A single completed result takes the perfective future: напишет.

items.promptEnglish: It will take me an hour to buy a gift.
items.hint: 'За час' frames a completed job. Which future fits?
items.explanation: За + accusative ('within an hour') frames completion, so the perfective future куплю fits.

blanks: Завтра Маша _____ статью к утру. (Tomorrow Masha will write the article by morning.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: 'К утру' (by morning) is a deadline cue, locking in the perfective. Perfective future, 3sg = напишет.

errorCorrection.sentence: Завтра я буду сделать всю работу за вечер.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Tomorrow I will do all the work in one evening.
errorCorrection.explanation: Буду plus an infinitive forms the imperfective future, so буду takes only an imperfective infinitive (буду делать). A perfective verb cannot use буду at all; its future is the one-word form сделаю, which the completion frame 'за вечер' calls for.

errorCorrection.sentence: С завтрашнего дня я погуляю в парке каждое утро.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Starting tomorrow, I will walk in the park every morning.
errorCorrection.explanation: A repeated future action ('every morning') is imperfective, and the imperfective future is the compound буду гулять. Perfective погуляю is the future of a single bounded stroll and cannot describe a daily routine.

errorCorrection.sentence: Сейчас я напишу письмо, не мешай.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Right now I am writing a letter, do not disturb me.
errorCorrection.explanation: The perfective has no present tense, so напишу is not 'I am writing' but the perfective future 'I will write (and finish).' For an action happening right now ('сейчас'), Russian uses the imperfective present пишу. Learners misread напишу as a present because its endings look present-tense, but a perfective conjugated form always points to the future.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I (m) will read the book through in an hour.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'За час' (in an hour) is a 'за + acc time' phrase from Lesson 5: completion. Perfective future: прочитаю (1sg). The imperfective 'буду читать' describes a process and clashes with 'за час.'

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha will read books every day.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Каждый день' (every day) is a habit cue from Lesson 4. Imperfective future: будет (3sg) + impf infinitive читать. The perfective прочитает would mark a single completed event, which 'каждый день' rules out.

reviewVocab.definition: future tense (Russian has two: imperfective буду + infinitive, and perfective conjugated forms of the perfective verb)
reviewVocab.example: В будущем времени два вида: я буду читать (НСВ) и я прочитаю (СВ).

reviewVocab.definition: 1sg form of быть in the future; auxiliary for the imperfective future (буду + impf infinitive)
reviewVocab.example: Я буду читать книгу весь вечер.

reviewVocab.definition: 1sg perfective future forms (present-conjugation forms of perfective verbs always have future meaning)
reviewVocab.example: Завтра я напишу письмо и прочитаю книгу.
